article_title: Automated Coding of Content and Pedagogical Content Knowledge of Mathematics Using a Multi-Agent Large Language Model
citation: Copur-Gencturk, Y., Moreno, K., Chu, Y., Li, H., & Tang, J. (2026). Automated coding of content and pedagogical content knowledge of mathematics using a multi-agent large language model. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01796-2
title: Two-domain conceptualization of mathematics teacher knowledge: CK and PCK with three PCK subdomains
description: The article's conceptual framework treats content-specific knowledge for teaching mathematics as two domains, CK and PCK. CK is understanding "the mathematical meaning of rules and strategies," connections among ideas, and reasoning and problem solving in the school curriculum, operationalized through proportional-reasoning items. PCK is conceptualized as content-specific pedagogy comprising three subdomains: knowledge of mathematical tasks, knowledge of students' mathematical thinking, and knowledge of teaching mathematics, each encompassing knowing as well as reasoning and application. This framework guided the development of the open-ended items that GradeOpt and the comparison models coded.
requirements: Items situated in teaching contexts, because the contextualized nature of PCK limits what multiple-choice items can capture
Coding manuals with construct descriptions, 3-point rubrics, and sample coded responses with justifications
constraints: The framework as operationalized here covers ratios and proportional relationships in middle school mathematics only
target_learning_goals: Measuring teachers' content knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge of ratios and proportional relationships
examples: The nine PCK items coded in the study comprised knowledge of mathematical tasks (2), knowledge of students' mathematical thinking (2), and knowledge of teaching mathematics (5), each scored with a 3-point rubric.
key_sources: Copur-Gencturk, Y., Moreno, K., Chu, Y., Li, H., & Tang, J. (2026). Automated coding of content and pedagogical content knowledge of mathematics using a multi-agent large language model. ZDM – Mathematics Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11858-026-01796-2

article_title: Using the C-K Theory to Develop Student's Creativity: A Case Study of Creative University
citation: Suacamram, M. (2019). Using the C-K theory to develop student's creativity: A Case Study of Creative University. International Journal of Instruction, 12(4), 719-732. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2019.12446a
title: C-K theory as a systematic framework for developing creativity through design
description: The C-K theory is a systematic practice for designing products, services or solutions by reviewing abstract ideas. It operates through two spaces: the Concept Space, which contains ideas that do not yet exist in the world, and the Knowledge Space, which contains existing information about techniques, commerce, society, rules and regulations. The design process involves four operators (K→C, C→C, K→K, C→K) that expand and transfer ideas between spaces. In this study, the theory was applied to create workshop lesson plans for developing creativity in film and design courses.
requirements: Teacher and students need to completely understand the process of C-K theory before applying it
constraints: Not appropriate for courses with fixed and unchangeable structures such as drawing, drafting, calculus, statistics
examples: Applied in a five-class 'Design and Visualization for Film' course covering photo design, problem identification, and film poster design
key_sources: Suacamram, M. (2019). Using the C-K theory to develop student's creativity: A Case Study of Creative University. International Journal of Instruction, 12(4), 719-732. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2019.12446a

article_title: Using the C-K Theory to Develop Student's Creativity: A Case Study of Creative University
citation: Suacamram, M. (2019). Using the C-K theory to develop student's creativity: A Case Study of Creative University. International Journal of Instruction, 12(4), 719-732. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2019.12446a
title: Five-class workshop sequence for developing creativity through C-K theory-based design projects
description: The lesson plans aim to develop learners' creativity through designing projects or other types of work activities based on C-K theory. The sequence consists of five classes: 1) photo design, 2) identifying and formulating problems, 3) reviewing problems, 4) creating a photo design based on C-K theory, and 5) designing a film poster based on C-K theory. Each class includes an introduction, main lesson, and wrap-up with assignments that progressively build creative design skills.
requirements: Content is suitable for third-year or higher undergraduate students who have passed general education courses and core courses of their major
target_learners: third-year undergraduate students majoring in Film
examples: Class 4 involved university students demonstrating C-K theory use and training high school students in self-portrait photography and toilet design
key_sources: Suacamram, M. (2019). Using the C-K theory to develop student's creativity: A Case Study of Creative University. International Journal of Instruction, 12(4), 719-732. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2019.12446a

article_title: Using the C-K Theory to Develop Student's Creativity: A Case Study of Creative University
citation: Suacamram, M. (2019). Using the C-K theory to develop student's creativity: A Case Study of Creative University. International Journal of Instruction, 12(4), 719-732. https://doi.org/10.29333/iji.2019.12446a
title: Teachers should consider the nature of assignments before applying C-K theory to enhance learners' creativity
description: The article identifies four guidelines for applying C-K theory to enhance creative development in undergraduate courses. Courses focusing on free design, design under certain obligations, and memorization are suitable for C-K theory application. However, courses that focus on practices and calculation cannot use C-K theory because their structure is fixed and unchangeable, preventing design of ideas in the Concept Space according to the imagination of the creators.
requirements: Teachers must understand the C-K theory process completely before applying it
constraints: Cannot be used in courses with fixed structures such as drawing, drafting, calculus, statistics
examples: Suitable courses include product design, project design, research, marketing strategic planning, laws, and history

article_title: Development and validation of a comprehensive tool to study the various elements influencing the utilization of E-learning among undergraduate health professions students.
citation: Kumar Archana Prabu, Mani Prabu Kumar Chokkalingam, Atta Komal, Omprakash Abirami, Maheshkumar K., Atwa Hany, Maruthy K. N., R. Padmavathi. (2025). Development and validation of a comprehensive tool to study the various elements influencing the utilization of E-learning among undergraduate health professions students. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07582-0
title: CKAPQ — Comprehensive Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Questionnaire for e-learning utilization
description: The CKAPQ is a psychometrically validated questionnaire assessing multiple dimensions of e-learning adoption among undergraduate medical and dental students. Developed via Zhou's Mixed Methods Model with focus groups and expert content validation (Lawshe method), it began as 59 items across eight theoretical factors and was refined to 16 items across five constructs. The article states it "provides a new, standardized method to evaluate knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to E-learning among medical and dental students" and can serve as a benchmarking tool for institutional assessment and educational policy development.
requirements: Administration to first-year medical and dental students; 5-point Likert response scale; content validation by experts with medical education degrees and technology-based education experience
constraints: Single-centre development at one South Indian university, limiting generalizability; focused on medical and dental education; relies on self-reported confidence, introducing potential subjective bias
target_learning_goals: assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to e-learning utilization
examples: Administered 2014–2017 via Moodle and institutional email to 1050 invited students, with 960 responding (91% response rate)
